checks.text: Typing "100000" in the field labelled "Principal", "5" in the field labelled "Annual rate %", and "30" in the field labelled "Years" shows "567.79" in the field labelled "Monthly payment".
With the same inputs as A1, the field labelled "Total interest" shows "104,403.60" and the field labelled "Total paid" shows "204,403.60".
Changing the field labelled "Years" to "15" updates the field labelled "Monthly payment" to "791.90" and the field labelled "Total interest" to "42,943.60".
With Principal "50000", Annual rate "0", and Years "5", the field labelled "Monthly payment" shows "833.33" and the field labelled "Total interest" shows "0.00".
Clicking the button labelled "Show schedule" reveals a table where the first data row contains "1" in the first column, "567.79" in the second column, and "417.79" in the third column.
In the schedule table from A5, the last data row contains "360" in the first column and "0.00" in the fourth column.
Typing "abc" in the field labelled "Principal" and pressing Tab shows the error message "Enter a valid number" and the field labelled "Monthly payment" remains empty.
Typing "-100" in the field labelled "Principal" and pressing Tab shows the error message "Principal must be positive" and the field labelled "Monthly payment" remains empty.
Reload keeps the calculated results: after entering Principal "100000", Annual rate "5", Years "30" and reloading, the field labelled "Monthly payment" still shows "567.79".
